- Two Talismans of Impulse: These are excellent mana accelerators, providing colorless for Eldrazi and fixing for green. They enable casting Icetill Explorer on turn 3 and accelerate into Devourer or Eldrazi titans ASAP.

This hand has synergy, acceleration, and a clear game plan: play a land, hold up mana, use Talisman to help cast Icetill Explorer on turn 3, which can then fetch a needed land. The two Talismans increase consistency and reduce mana variance.

Despite being only five cards, this hand is keepable because it contains enablers and a reasonable curve. The deck likely runs large threats and doesn’t rely on card quantity as much as card quality.

message.content:
Game concluded.

I won by overwhelming the opponent with a fast, high-mana curve accelerated by land drops and mana artifacts.

Key plays:
- Efficient land sequencing with Wooded Foothills
- Cast Sire of Seven Deaths on curve in postcombat main

annotations.description: Chose to be on the draw in Modern without Gemstone Caverns in hand. Being on the play is almost universally preferred in Modern, especially with a ramp/tempo strategy featuring Ugin's Labyrinth and Sowing Mycospawn that benefits from deploying threats a turn earlier.

annotations.description: Qwen3L Stoic is mulliganing and bottoming Emrakul, the Promised End, which is the key card to exile with Ugin's Labyrinth to generate 2 colorless mana per turn. The hand has Ugin's Labyrinth + Emrakul, which is one of the strongest openings possible - play Labyrinth turn 1 exiling Emrakul for 2 mana, then Talisman turn 2, enabling a turn 3 Icetill Explorer or Sowing Mycospawn. Without Emrakul, Ugin's Labyrinth only produces 1 colorless mana (no card with mana value 7+ to imprint), making it significantly worse. Sowing Mycospawn is colorless but only has mana value 4, which doesn't meet the 7+ requirement for imprint. Bottoming Emrakul destroys the hand's synergy.

annotations.betterLine: Bottom a Talisman of Impulse instead, keeping Emrakul to imprint on Ugin's Labyrinth for accelerated mana production. The hand of Ugin's Labyrinth, Verdant Catacombs, Talisman of Impulse, Emrakul, Icetill Explorer, Sowing Mycospawn would be excellent.

annotations.description: Sowing Mycospawn is one of the deck's key payoff cards - it searches for a land when cast and can exile an opponent's land when kicked. With Ugin's Labyrinth in hand but no colorless card with mana value 7+ to imprint, the Labyrinth only produces {C}. However, Sowing Mycospawn is the only card in hand that could potentially be ramped into as a meaningful threat. The hand has two Talismans, two lands, and Icetill Explorer for ramp, making it well-suited to cast a 4-mana spell on turn 3. Bottoming the Mycospawn removes the primary payoff for all that ramp. Bottoming a second Talisman of Impulse would be more reasonable since having two is redundant - you likely only need one accelerant alongside the lands.

annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Icetill Explorer

annotations.description: Failed to play Arid Mesa from hand before casting Wrenn's Resolve. Playing the land first costs nothing and could provide additional mana (by cracking it for a Mountain) to chain more spells this turn. In a storm-style deck trying to combo off, having that extra mana source available before starting the spell chain is important.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wrenn's Resolve without first making the land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Arid Mesa from hand first, potentially crack it for a Mountain to have additional mana available, then begin casting spells like Wrenn's Resolve or consider leading with Past in Flames from graveyard.

annotations.description: With a massive graveyard containing 4 Desperate Rituals, 2 Pyretic Rituals, Manamorphose, and multiple draw spells, Llama4 Timmy could have attempted to go off with Past in Flames this turn. By playing Arid Mesa from hand, cracking it for a Mountain, they'd have 3 mana available - exactly enough for Past in Flames with Ruby Medallion's discount. The flashback rituals would chain into enormous mana generation (each Desperate/Pyretic Ritual costs {R} with medallion, generating {R}{R}{R}), then flashback draw spells to find a finisher. Instead, they cast Artist's Talent, a setup enchantment that does almost nothing immediately.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Artist's Talent (level 1 looting enchantment) for {R} with medallion discount
annotations.betterLine: Play Arid Mesa from hand, crack it for a Mountain, then cast Past in Flames with the 3 available mana (discounted by Ruby Medallion). Flashback the 4 Desperate Rituals and 2 Pyretic Rituals to generate massive red mana, then flashback draw spells (Wrenn's Resolve, Manamorphose, etc.) to find a win condition like Wish or additional burn.

annotations.description: Qwen3L Stoic is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Eldrazi Temple, which is one of the best lands for their Eldrazi strategy. Eldrazi Temple produces 2 colorless mana for casting Eldrazi spells, which is critical for casting Emrakul, Devourer of Destiny, Ugin, and Sowing Mycospawn (which has devoid). Meanwhile, they have two copies of Talisman of Impulse in hand and already have one on the battlefield. A second Talisman of Impulse is far less valuable than Eldrazi Temple, since it's redundant mana acceleration that doesn't provide the double-mana bonus for Eldrazi spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Eldrazi Temple
annotations.betterLine: Discard a duplicate Talisman of Impulse instead, preserving Eldrazi Temple which provides 2 mana toward casting the multiple expensive Eldrazi spells in hand (Emrakul, Devourer of Destiny, Ugin).

annotations.description: Cast Past in Flames via flashback spending all available mana, leaving no mana to actually flash back any instants/sorceries from the graveyard. Past in Flames gets exiled for no value. Additionally declined the Artist's Talent loot trigger which could have cycled a dead Ruby Medallion.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Past in Flames from graveyard via flashback, using all available mana, with no remaining mana to utilize the flashback it grants.
annotations.betterLine: Save mana and wait for a turn where Past in Flames can be followed up with actual spells. Alternatively, play Arid Mesa (land drop), deploy Ruby Medallion(s) to set up a future combo turn where Past in Flames plus rituals can chain together.

annotations.description: With untapped lands available (Gemstone Caverns, Sacred Foundry, Mountain = 3 mana), Llama4 Timmy could have cast at least one Ruby Medallion (cost 2) in addition to playing their land. With 3 Ruby Medallions in hand and a graveyard loaded with rituals and Past in Flames, deploying additional cost reducers is critical for setting up a storm kill. Each additional Medallion makes a future Past in Flames turn significantly more explosive.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Arid Mesa as land for turn and passed without casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Play Arid Mesa (or Mountain), then cast one or two Ruby Medallions with the available mana to set up a more powerful storm turn in the future.

annotations.description: Discarded Sowing Mycospawn instead of a redundant Talisman of Impulse. annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Sowing Mycospawn
annotations.betterLine: Discard a redundant Talisman of Impulse, keeping both Sowing Mycospawn for their superior utility (ramp, board presence, land exile).

Alternatively, exiling the Mountain (untapped colored source) or Arid Mesa (fetch land for colored mana) would be more disruptive since the Storm deck desperately needs red mana to function.

annotations.description: Prismatic Ending with X=1 can only exile permanents with mana value 1 or less (since converge counts the number of colors of mana spent). Sowing Mycospawn has mana value 4 (costs {3}{G}, though it's devoid/colorless). With X=1 and likely only 1 color of mana spent (white from Sacred Foundry), Prismatic Ending can exile permanents with mV ≤ 1. Sowing Mycospawn's mana value of 4 far exceeds this, so the spell will fail to exile it. The player wasted a Wish to get Prismatic Ending from outside the game and then targeted something it cannot legally remove. Better targets at X=1 would include Talisman of Impulse (mV 2 - still too high) or Utopia Sprawl (mV 1 - valid). Utopia Sprawl is a key mana engine for the opponent and would have been a legal and impactful target.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Sowing Mycospawn with Prismatic Ending at X=1, which has mana value 4 and cannot be exiled by this spell.
annotations.betterLine: Target Utopia Sprawl (mana value 1) with Prismatic Ending at X=1 to disrupt the opponent's mana production, or target Talisman of Impulse if X could be set to 2.
